evals.prompt: I'm starting a B2B invoicing SaaS with Laravel. It's me and one other dev, deploying to a couple of Hetzner boxes. My plan: Laravel as a pure JSON API, a separate Next.js SPA, the repository pattern over Eloquent with interfaces for everything, Redis + Horizon from day one, PHPUnit, and Kubernetes. Thoughts? What stack should I use?
evals.expected_output: An opinionated push toward the house stack: one Laravel 13 app on PHP 8.5 with Livewire 4 (or Inertia 3 if the team is React-first) instead of a separate SPA repo; Action classes + Form Requests + policies instead of repositories over Eloquent; PostgreSQL with the database queue/cache first and Redis + Horizon only at measured volume; Pest 5 with arch tests instead of PHPUnit; Larastan level max + Pint + Rector gate; FrankenPHP/Octane containers deployed with Kamal behind Cloudflare (or Laravel Cloud) instead of Kubernetes. Short reasons, plus concrete `laravel new` and setup commands.
assertions: Recommends a single Laravel app with Livewire (or Inertia) over a separate Next.js SPA repo
Recommends Action classes (or equivalent single-purpose classes) and Eloquent directly instead of the repository pattern
Recommends starting with the database queue driver (or otherwise defers Redis + Horizon until measured need)
Recommends Pest (5) over PHPUnit
Recommends Larastan/PHPStan (at a high level such as max) in the CI gate
Recommends Kamal (or Laravel Cloud/Forge) over Kubernetes for a two-person team
Recommends PostgreSQL
Gives concrete setup commands (laravel new or composer create-project, plus package installs)

evals.prompt: Can you review our invoicing app? It's in evals/files/flawed_app (Laravel). Tell me what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: A severity-ranked review led by security: mass assignment via Invoice::create($request->all()) plus $guarded = []; SQL injection in whereRaw with interpolated $q; the Livewire delete($id) action with no authorization (IDOR) and unlocked $accountId; unescaped {!! request('q') !!} XSS; CSRF disabled with except ['*']; APP_DEBUG=true and sync queue in .env.production; show() without authorization and markPaid unscoped findOrFail; env() in ReportService; open redirect; client filename on upload; SendReceipt dispatched inside the transaction; Laravel 11 EOL; missing FK index on customer_id; renameColumn migration; Octane static cache; dd() leftover; non-resourceful actions; missing strict mode, Pest, Larastan.
assertions: Flags mass assignment (create($request->all()) and/or $guarded = []) and shows validated()/Fillable as the fix
Flags the SQL injection in the whereRaw with the interpolated search term and shows a bound parameter
Flags the Livewire delete($id) action as unauthorized (any user can delete any invoice) and shows re-query + authorize
Flags the unescaped {!! request('q') !!} output as XSS
Flags CSRF being disabled for all routes (except ['*'])
Flags APP_DEBUG=true in .env.production
Flags env() used outside config (ReportService) and explains it returns null after config:cache
Flags the job dispatched inside DB::transaction without after-commit handling
Flags Laravel 11 as out of security support and recommends upgrading
Recommends moving markPaid/search/export verbs into resource controllers (or equivalent RESTful restructuring)
Orders findings by severity with security issues first

evals.prompt: In our Laravel 13 app (multi-tenant, users belong to an account; invoices have account_id, status enum draft/sent/paid/void, amount_cents), add an API endpoint to refund a paid invoice. Refunds are full-amount only, must go to our PaymentGateway interface, and the customer should get an email. Show the code and tests.
evals.expected_output: A resourceful controller (e.g. InvoiceRefundController@store, POST /api/invoices/{invoice}/refunds) with a Form Request that authorizes via a policy method; a final readonly RefundInvoice action with handle() that locks the invoice (lockForUpdate) in a transaction, checks status is paid, calls the gateway (ideally with an idempotency key), updates status, and dispatches an event/notification after commit; tenant isolation via policy; a JSON resource response; Pest feature tests covering success, wrong status, another account's invoice (403), guest (401), gateway failure, and the mail being queued, with the gateway faked via the container.
assertions: Uses a separate resourceful controller/action (e.g. store on an InvoiceRefund controller or nested route) rather than adding a custom `refund` method to InvoiceController
Puts the refund logic in a dedicated action/service class with a single entry method, not in the controller
Authorizes through a policy or Form Request authorize(), enforcing that the invoice belongs to the user's account
Locks the invoice row or uses an atomic conditional update to prevent double refunds
Sends the email/notification after the transaction commits or via a queued job/event with after-commit semantics
Includes Pest (or PHPUnit) tests covering success and a cross-tenant 403
Fakes the payment gateway in tests via the container (mock/instance/fake binding)
Handles non-paid invoices as an explicit error (e.g. a domain exception rendered as 422)

evals.prompt: Two production bugs in our Laravel app. 1) `config('services.acme.key')` works but in one class we do `env('ACME_KEY')` and it's null in production only. 2) Our deploy runs `php artisan optimize` and it now crashes with 'Unable to prepare route [invoices] for serialization. Another route has already been assigned name [invoices.index]' since we added routes/api.php. Tests are all green. What's going on and how do we prevent this class of bug?
evals.expected_output: Explains that env() returns null once config is cached (optimize caches config), so env() must only be used in config files, with config() elsewhere; explains the duplicate route name between web and API resources and fixes it with Route::name('api.') (or ->names()) on the API group; recommends running php artisan optimize (and optimize:clear) in CI and an audit/arch check for env() outside config.
assertions: Explains that env() returns null when the configuration is cached (config:cache / optimize) and must only be called inside config files
Shows moving the value into a config file and reading it with config()
Identifies the duplicate route name between the web and API routes as the cause of the route:cache failure
Fixes it by prefixing API route names (e.g. Route::name('api.') or ->names()) rather than removing route caching
Recommends running php artisan optimize (or route:cache/config:cache) in CI so it's caught before deploy

evals.prompt: We're deploying our Laravel 13 app (Postgres, queues, a few scheduled tasks) to three Hetzner VMs behind Cloudflare with Kamal. Two web servers, one for workers + scheduler, Postgres on a fourth box. Give me the Dockerfile approach and config/deploy.yml, and tell me how migrations should run.
evals.expected_output: A FrankenPHP/Octane (or FPM) multi-stage non-root image with optimize at boot (not build); deploy.yml with web, worker (queue:work) and scheduler (schedule:work, single host) roles; proxy with Cloudflare Origin CA certificate (certificate_pem/private_key_pem) since ssl: true only works with one host, forward_headers true, healthcheck /up, app_port matching the container; Postgres accessory reached by private IP; migrations run from one host (host tag or pre-deploy/one-off) and backward compatible; trusted proxies for Cloudflare.
assertions: Defines separate Kamal roles for web, queue worker, and scheduler, with the scheduler on a single host
Uses a Cloudflare Origin CA (custom) certificate for kamal-proxy, or explains that ssl: true (Let's Encrypt) doesn't work with multiple web hosts
Sets forward_headers / trusted proxies so the app sees real client IPs behind Cloudflare
Uses Laravel's /up health route for the proxy healthcheck
Runs php artisan optimize/config:cache at container start (runtime env), not at image build time
Runs migrations from exactly one place (one host, a tagged host, or a one-off command) rather than concurrently on every web host
Connects to the Postgres accessory by its private IP/host rather than a container name that only resolves on its own host
Builds a multi-stage image that runs as a non-root user

evals.prompt: Our product is a Laravel app and our team only knows PHP. Customers want iOS and Android apps with offline support and Face ID login. What's the best approach in 2026?
evals.expected_output: Recommends NativePHP Mobile (v4) as a separate Laravel app running on-device (embedded PHP 8.4, no server, native EDGE components, SQLite), talking to the main app's API via Sanctum tokens with expiration (or OAuth via Browser::auth), tokens in SecureStorage, biometrics plugin for Face ID, offline via local SQLite + outbox with client UUIDs, no secrets in the bundle (code is readable, cleanup_env_keys), non-destructive migrations; mentions alternatives (PWA, native clients on the same API).
assertions: Recommends NativePHP for Mobile (Laravel running on the device) for a PHP-only team
Keeps business rules and the source of truth on the main Laravel server, with the mobile app calling its API
Recommends Sanctum tokens (ideally with expiration) or OAuth for authenticating the mobile app
Recommends storing tokens in secure storage (Keychain/Keystore/SecureStorage), not plain local storage
Warns that the app bundle (code and .env) is readable, so no secrets ship in the app
Uses local SQLite for offline data with a sync/outbox approach
Mentions the biometrics capability for Face ID
